metadata.title: Providing Quality Early Childhood Education and Care: Results from the Starting Strong Survey 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS Starting Strong report is based on the Starting Strong survey of ECEC staff and centre leaders, designed to approximate quality through questionnaire responses. The document describes the survey’s conceptual framework (process and structural aspects of quality) and the use of staff/leader questionnaires, but it does not provide the technical sampling/weighting variable names or replicate-weight procedures in the excerpt provided. For analysts using the underlying TALIS Starting Strong microdata, complex survey design features (stratification/clustering) are typically handled via the survey weights supplied with the dataset; however, this report text does not specify whether those weights were applied in the reported descriptive results. Because the excerpt does not include the dataset technical documentation, the exact weight variable (e.g., a student/centre weight) and any replicate-weight method cannot be confirmed from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive policy report summarising results from the TALIS Starting Strong survey rather than an empirical predictive modelling study with a clearly specified PV-based cognitive outcome. The excerpt does not report any plausible-values generation/combination procedure, and it also does not document a missing-data handling strategy for an ML pipeline. As a result, plausible values are not applicable to the extraction target here, and missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the TALIS Starting Strong 2018 survey of ECEC staff and centre leaders to produce cross-country results; the excerpt does not specify the analytic inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., centre/staff eligibility, response completeness thresholds, or any country-level restrictions).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS Starting Strong report synthesises evidence on early childhood education and care (ECEC) quality by surveying ECEC staff and centre leaders. It frames quality through two dimensions: process aspects (e.g., daily interactions between staff and children) and structural aspects (e.g., staff education/training, classroom/playroom environment, and monitoring mechanisms). The report highlights relationships between staff pre-service and in-service education/training and working conditions and the practices staff use with children and parents, and it documents cross-country and within-country variation in workforce characteristics and quality-related factors. It also reports bottlenecks perceived by staff and leaders, including staff absences and shortages, and priorities for professional development and spending reallocation (e.g., support for children with special needs, reducing group size). The excerpt does not provide technical details on sampling weights, plausible values, missing-data handling, or any predictive modelling metrics, so the results should be interpreted as survey-based descriptive/policy evidence rather than ML performance claims.
